chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muawiya ibn Maythara said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling the palm trees for two years. He said, 'There is no harm in it.' I said, 'And the rutbah (fresh dates), we sell this portion, and so and so portion after it.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.' Then he said, 'My father used to sell the henna in such and such batches.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling palm trees and fresh dates in portions according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility (*ibahah*) of selling unripe fruit (*thamar*) for extended periods, specifically citing the sale of palm trees for two years and fresh dates in installments. It reinforces this ruling by referencing the practical precedent of the Imams, noting that Imam al-Sadiq’s father (Imam al-Baqir) engaged in similar bulk sales of henna, thereby validating flexible commercial contracts in Shia jurisprudence.
